mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day windows where both triggers are met (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200K for two consecutive months indicates cooling demand, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain non-negative during confirmed cooling periods (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month is interpreted as supply-side weakness, reducing future capacity utilization and generating negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 3% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during prior supply expansions (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a tightening cycle, investors anticipate future rate hikes, causing a sharp discounting of equity valuations and a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative when inflation crosses above 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in wage growth (implied by UNRATE trends) suggest labor market softening, which can depress consumer sentiment and equity valuations, yielding negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE remains flat or rises
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during periods of robust wage growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a placeholder for demand proxies) would indicate weakening demand, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns. This sketch demonstrates the structure for demand proxies even if not directly available in the evidence set.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by > 2% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not negative when demand proxy falls (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3% for two months), the present value of future cash flows is expected to rise, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than during pre-easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).
